## 2. What it leans on

- **morale_diff** 0.828 (was 0.811): own minus enemy morale summed over players (boosts +, death penalty -)
- **knights_diff** 0.367 (was 0.414): own minus enemy pit knights alive
- **footmen_lost_diff** 0.322 (was 0.339): own minus enemy footmen lost so far (base NPCs, not pit NPCs). Proposed 2026-11-06 from OG comms ([ohno v NwAy]: 'this way we don't lose footmen'); moved in as footmen alive after chunk 4, then counted as losses after chunk 5 (Denning): a footman only enters the replay once something touches it, so 'alive' marked a base that was visited and read backwards (-42 points at +4); deaths are always recorded
- **morale_diff & map_bases_apart** 0.275 (new): own minus enemy morale summed over players (boosts +, death penalty -) TOGETHER WITH the map's distance between the two bases
- **stand** 0.199 (was 0.22): who holds the flag stand: 1 own, 0 nobody, -1 enemy
- **spike_killable_diff** 0.194 (was 0.119): enemy minus own players within one spike of the other side (DP stacking; 0 unless a spike build is involved)
- **fight_state** 0.19 (was 0.153): who is winning the fight now: enemy minus own expected deaths in the next 10 s, from a deaths model that never saw the match (fightstate.py)
- **lord_dps_own** 0.186 (was 0.172): own build's measured Lord damage per second if all its non-healers were at the Lord
- **lord_dps_enemy** 0.185 (was 0.171): enemy build's measured Lord damage per second
- **flag_lead** 0.159 (was 0.174): seconds up (+) or down (-) on flags: enemy's response minus own on the next capture exchange
- **lord_damage_diff & map_bases_apart** 0.145 (was 0.074): own minus enemy Lord damage dealt so far (the 28:00 tiebreak; players can't see it); blank when either team's Lord damage wasn't observed TOGETHER WITH the map's distance between the two bases
- **morale_diff & map_flag_run** 0.142 (new): own minus enemy morale summed over players (boosts +, death penalty -) TOGETHER WITH the map's flag run Y: distance from the flag spawn to the stand (average of both sides)

## 7. The usual play

Each choice against the most common one in that kind of decision, in win-chance points over the decision's window, adjusted for the situation, with a 90% range from resampling whole matches. CLEAR = the range excludes 0. Win chance comes from a model that never saw the match. The same comparison over the 30 s BEFORE the decision is a placebo test: a choice can't cause what came before it, so a clear difference there means the effect is partly who makes that choice.

## Does the advice work? (the goal test)

For each decision kind, the advice is built from five groups of matches and read on the sixth (unseen): teams whose choice matched the advice against teams whose didn't, win-chance change over the decision's window adjusted for the situation, 90% range from resampling whole matches. The advice = the best choice among the 15 most similar decisions (at least 5 cases, 2+ points better than the usual play), else the usual play. "Specific" = the advice differed from the usual play.

**4 of 13 kinds pass** (effect positive, range excludes 0): after_wipe, power_play, runner_choice, split_or_stay.

- after_wipe (1037 decisions, 423 matches): matched the advice 74% of the time; effect of matching +3.5 points (90% +2.2 to +5.3; clear); raw 0.5 matched against -2.9 not; specific advice in 6% of cases, raw effect there +7.2. Most recommended: pushed the pit (957), took the flag (55), reset (25).
- boost_clock (1665 decisions, 419 matches): matched the advice 21% of the time; effect of matching -0.4 points (90% -1.2 to +0.4; not clear); raw -0.7 matched against -0.4 not; specific advice in 1% of cases. Most recommended: not running, fought (559), running, advanced (291), running, fought (240), not running, fell back (239), not running, advanced (178), running, fell back (79).
- eight_v_eight_or_flag (3967 decisions, 409 matches): matched the advice 73% of the time; effect of matching +0.1 points (90% -0.9 to +0.9; not clear); raw -0.5 matched against -1.1 not; specific advice in 11% of cases, raw effect there +2.0. Most recommended: flag game (3301), commit all 8 (666).
- enemy_pickup (5518 decisions, 426 matches): matched the advice 22% of the time; effect of matching -1.0 points (90% -2.0 to +0.2; not clear); raw -1.0 matched against -0.1 not; specific advice in 1% of cases, raw effect there +1.4. Most recommended: already running, advanced (1041), held, fell back (844), held, advanced (808), already running, fell back (744), held, fought (683), already running, fought (599).
- late_game (156 decisions, 78 matches): matched the advice 53% of the time; effect of matching +4.9 points (90% -2.5 to +11.1; not clear); raw 1.7 matched against -3.0 not; specific advice in 37% of cases, raw effect there +8.1. Most recommended: 2 to 3 at the enemy Lord (83), 0 to 1 at the enemy Lord (47), 4+ at the enemy Lord (26).
- npcs_or_dp (263 decisions, 204 matches): matched the advice 65% of the time; effect of matching +1.4 points (90% -0.3 to +3.2; not clear); raw 0.7 matched against -0.4 not; specific advice in 5% of cases. Most recommended: NPCs (199), DP (36), both (28).

## 8. What results and causes are worth

Win points for the team it happened to, from 446 matches. **Result** = how matches actually ended against what a win model that never saw the match expected just before (so it includes what the event usually led to); **model** = the win model's own change over the next 30 s. Both against matched moments without the event (same minute and win chance). A gap between the two points at a win-model curve to check.

Context (strength, build skill counts, flag lead, morale, the clock) is left out: it describes the situation, it is not a cause to fix.

## The TQs

Denning's four questions, each from the batch's matches. The why comes from forensics and events (every number placed against the same role or situation in every stored match); the different play comes only from measurement: the usual play's choice effects (usual.py), node models read again with the variable changed (models that never saw the match, changes priced in win points with values.py), options that were ready and unused, and benchmarks. Points = win-chance points.

## TQ 1. Behind on flags

*The biggest flag swing in the new matches: push +80 -> -79 by 14:50.0.*

### Flag swing: push v chic (15522caa), 12:00.0 to 14:50.0
**Result**: push's flag lead +80 s -> -79 s (-159 s). Stand: push -> chic.
